page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores mapped directly to 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, providing 1.0 thread per core. Memory capacity totals 64 GB RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting instruction sets like AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, while omitting AVX-512 and matrix extensions. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached persistent disks, and no hardware GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent compute capabilities typical of AMD Zen 3 execution cores. In synthetic CPU-focused evaluations, the instance achieves a strong single-core stress-ng score of 2,695.28 alongside an average multi-core output of 43,100.81. Geekbench testing delivers a single-core score of 1,519.0 and a multi-core score of 12,216.0, registering steady performance across Clang software compilation (20,037.0) and ray tracing tasks (24,580.0). Memory evaluations show an uncached read bandwidth of 86.62 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 49.13 GB/sec. Across networked workloads, the configuration sustains 29.42 million Redis SET operations per second, a web serving throughput of 18.9 GB/sec, and a strong text generation rate of 306.6 tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter language models.

Because each vCPU corresponds to an unshared physical core rather than a shared hyperthread, the t2d-standard-16 delivers predictable runtime performance free from thread contention. This architectural layout enhances qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out infrastructure, though the absence of integrated NVMe storage requires factoring in external network storage latency. The lack of AVX-512 extensions also limits specialized vector mathematical calculations. The instance is suited for multi-tier web serving, continuous integration compilation runners, Redis caching nodes, and mid-tier database hosting.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with a 16-core AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture and 64 GB of memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Built with 16 dedicated physical cores operating at one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers reliable single-tenant core execution. The processor features 32 MB of L3 cache, AVX vector support, and cryptographic extensions, but excludes AVX-512 instructions. The server includes no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. In synthetic evaluations, it records strong single-thread performance in stress-ng and lightweight language model generation, along with solid multi-core execution in Clang compilation and PassMark testing. With uncached read bandwidth reaching 86.62 GB/sec and high Redis throughput, the instance is configured for web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and relational databases.
